title: What does it mean to trust someone?
examples: What is trust in a friendship?
How do I get my friend to trust me again?
How do you know if you can trust someone?

explain.say: Imagine a jar. Every time a friend keeps their word, one marble drops in. That jar is trust. Now look at the circle on the board. It starts right here, when you keep a promise.

faq.a: By doing what you say, being honest, keeping private things private, and being kind when someone shares a worry. Each small kept promise adds a marble to the jar.
asks: Tell me about the Keep a promise

faq.a: Reliable means people can count on you. If you say you will come at four, you come at four.
asks: Tell me about the Trust grows

faq.q: What do you do if you broke someone's trust?
faq.a: Say sorry honestly, explain what you will do differently, and then show it again and again. Trust comes back through actions more than words.
asks: How do I fix a friendship after I let someone down?

faq.a: Often yes, but it takes time. Each kept promise is like putting a marble back in the jar.
asks: Will my friend ever trust me again?

faq.q: Should I always keep a friend's secret?
faq.a: Keep kind, private things, like who they have a crush on. But if a secret means someone is being hurt or is in danger, telling a trusted adult is the right thing to do.
asks: Is it ever okay to tell a secret?

facts: The researcher Brené Brown describes trust as a marble jar that is filled slowly by small trustworthy actions.
Psychologists describe trust as being willing to rely on someone because you expect them to act well towards you.

wrong.1: Sharing a friend's private fear breaks trust.
